 Sensex at 95,000 or 1 lakh? Morgan Stanley says India’s 3D engine is putting stocks at an inflexion point
 SECTIONS Sensex at 95,000 or 1 lakh? Morgan Stanley says India’s 3D engine is putting stocks at an inflexion point By Nikhil Agarwal , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 02:30:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Morgan Stanley sees the Sensex rising 16% to 95,000 by December 2027, with a bull-case target of 1,05,000. The brokerage cites India's durable, diversified and decoupled growth, an improving earnings cycle and strong domestic flows as key drivers, while flagging elevated oil prices and global slowdown risks.

 Agencies India’s stock market could be entering a decisive phase, with Morgan Stanley forecasting a 16% rise in the Sensex by December 2027 and setting out a bull case target that takes the index above 1 lakh. The brokerage’s base case target for the BSE Sensex is 95,000, implying 16% upside from current levels. Its bull case target is 1,05,000, while the bear case scenario sees the index falling to 68,000.
 Morgan Stanley said Indian stocks appear to be at an “inflexion point” and could perform significantly better next year. The brokerage described India’s advantage as a “3D edge” — durable, diversified and decoupled growth.
The probability weighted outcome for December 2027 is 90,750, according to the report.

 Earnings cycle gains traction 
The central pillar of Morgan Stanley’s bullish outlook is an improving earnings cycle. The brokerage projects Sensex earnings to compound at approximately 18% through FY29. Its top down estimates point to Sensex earnings per share of 4,081 in FY27, 4,871 in FY28 and 5,669 in FY29.
 Live Events
 That implies earnings growth of 18.5% in FY27, 19.4% in FY28 and 16.4% in FY29. Broad market earnings growth is forecast at 20% in FY27, 23% in FY28 and 20% in FY29.
 Morgan Stanley said India’s earnings growth cycle is gaining traction, making the gap between India’s earnings outlook and that of the rest of the world a key factor for market performance in 2027.
 The brokerage also expects the profit-to-GDP ratio to reach new highs before the end of the decade.
 Also Read | Nifty profit growth hits 17-quarter high at 27%, upgrades now outpace downgrades. Is earnings cycle turning? 
 Why Morgan Stanley is bullish 
Morgan Stanley’s outlook is supported by what it describes as India’s durable domestic growth, diversified economic structure and relative insulation from global shocks.
High frequency indicators remain strong, while investment is projected to rise to 37.5% of GDP over the next five years. Monetary policy support, an undervalued currency, limited fiscal headwinds and robust consumer sentiment are also supporting the outlook, the brokerage said.
India’s equity market could also benefit if the global artificial-intelligence capital-expenditure cycle loses momentum or geopolitical tensions ease. Morgan Stanley said either development could increase India’s relative appeal.
The brokerage expects robust domestic growth, steady global growth, a resolution to the India-US trade deal and Brent crude below $100 a barrel in its base case.
It also expects domestic equity flows to remain strong, supported by a nascent IPO pipeline and retail demand staying ahead of equity supply. Foreign positioning in India is at an all-time low, according to the report.
 Sensex at 1 lakh in the bull case 
Morgan Stanley’s December 2027 Sensex target of 95,000 implies a trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 23 times. That is above the index’s 25-year average of 22 times.
The premium reflects greater confidence in India’s medium-term growth cycle, lower market beta, a higher terminal growth rate and a more predictable policy environment, the brokerage said.
The base case carries a 50% probability and assumes robust domestic growth, steady global growth, resolution of the India-US trade deal and Brent crude below $100 a barrel. Morgan Stanley projects Sensex earnings to compound at 18.1% through fiscal 2029 in this scenario.
The bull case, assigned a 30% probability, puts the Sensex at 1,05,000. This scenario assumes oil prices remain below $75 a barrel, supply-side pressures ease, inflation estimates decline, long-term capital gains tax rates are reduced to zero and other reforms improve flows into the economy and markets.
In the bull case, Sensex earnings compound at 20.3% annually between FY26 and FY29.
 What could derail the rally? 
Morgan Stanley’s bear case carries a 20% probability and places the Sensex at 68,000, implying a 17% decline from current levels.
That scenario assumes crude oil rises above $100 a barrel and remains there for several months, the Reserve Bank of India tightens policy to protect macroeconomic stability and global growth slows meaningfully.
In that case, Sensex earnings would compound at 15.8% annually through FY29, with growth slowing perceptibly over the next 12 months. Equity valuations would also de-rate to reflect weaker macroeconomic conditions.
The brokerage identified a bunching of new equity issues, renewed supply-side inflation pressures, oil prices exceeding $120 a barrel and a major global growth slowdown as key risks.
